scenarios.title: An Agent Calls
text: A man called {A} has been watching his matches. He has a nice watch, a business card and a list of players he 'looks after'. He promises a move abroad within two years.
{A}, an agent who represents three national-team players, sends a message: 'You're better than your club. Let me prove it.'
scenarios.prompt: An agent wants to represent you.

choices.label: Sign with {A}
choices.hint: Doors open. A cut goes out.
choices.text: He signs. {Al} starts making calls the same afternoon. Within a month, two scouts are at his matches.

out.text: The players he represents say he's honest and tough. He signs with confidence.
One player says {Al} took thirty per cent of his signing fee. He passes.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.text: He says not yet. {Al} leaves his card. 'You'll call.'

scenarios.title: A Super-Agent
scenarios.text: {A}, one of the most powerful agents in world football, wants to take him from his current agent. 'Your man is small-time. I make players global.'

choices.label: Switch to {A}
choices.hint: Your old agent may sue. Your new one takes more.
choices.text: He switches. His old agent sends a lawyer's letter and a very sad voice note. {Al} gets him a sponsor meeting within a week.

choices.label: Stay loyal
choices.desc: He's been with you since the start.
choices.text: He stays. His agent finds out and works twice as hard for him.

scenarios.title: The Numbers Don't Add Up
scenarios.text: His accountant flags something: commissions taken twice, a 'consultancy fee' to a company in {Al}'s wife's name, a signing bonus that seems smaller than it should be.
scenarios.prompt: Your agent may be stealing from you.

out.text: {Al} admits it, blames a 'misunderstanding' and pays most of it back. Trust gone.
{Al} denies everything and threatens to sue for defamation. He has better lawyers.

choices.label: Fire him and go to the authorities
choices.text: He fires {Al} and files a complaint with the federation. It takes two years. Some of the money comes back.

scenarios.title: The Small Print
scenarios.text: Reading his contract properly for the first time, he finds a clause he didn't know about: the club can extend his deal by a year without his agreement.
scenarios.prompt: A hidden clause in your contract.

choices.label: Ask your agent to challenge it
choices.text: His agent challenges it. The club agrees to remove it in exchange for a smaller raise next year.

choices.label: Learn from it
choices.text: He hires a lawyer to read every contract from now on. Expensive, sensible.

scenarios.title: Free Boots
scenarios.text: A boot company's local rep offers him free boots for a year if he wears them in matches. No money, just boots. For a kid who used to share boots with his cousin, it feels enormous.
scenarios.prompt: Your first boot deal: free boots.

choices.label: Accept gratefully
choices.text: Six pairs of boots arrive in a box. He photographs them like a trophy. {MUM} keeps the box.

choices.label: Ask for a small fee too

out.text: The rep laughs and adds a tiny fee. Respect for asking.
The rep withdraws the offer. Lesson learned.

scenarios.title: Small Wages
scenarios.text: His first wage barely covers rent, food and the bus to training. Some of the older players drive expensive cars. He counts coins for the bus.

choices.label: Live very cheaply and save
choices.text: Rice, eggs, the bus, a shared room. He saves a little every month. It's the best financial habit he'll ever form.

choices.label: Ask {DAD} for help
choices.text: {DAD} sends money he doesn't have. {J} promises himself he'll pay it back ten times over.

choices.label: Borrow from a teammate
choices.text: A senior player lends him money with no deadline. It creates a bond, and a quiet obligation.

scenarios.title: The Club Flat
scenarios.text: The club puts its young players in a shared flat. {J} is sharing with {T}, who plays the same position, snores like a motorbike and steals his food.

choices.label: Make it work, become friends
choices.text: They cook terrible meals together and watch films until 2am. Rivals on the pitch, brothers at home.

choices.label: Set strict rules
choices.text: Labels on everything. The stealing stops. So does the warmth.

scenarios.title: Someone in the Stands
scenarios.text: A man in a long coat is in the stands with a notebook. The kit man whispers: 'Scout. From abroad.' Suddenly everyone is playing for the man in the coat.

choices.label: Play your normal game
choices.text: He plays his normal game. The scout writes three lines about him and leaves at half-time. Normal is good.

out.text: A moment of magic in the 60th minute. The scout stops writing and just watches.
He tries too much and loses the ball six times. The scout leaves early.

scenarios.title: Too Many Brands
scenarios.text: Sponsor duties take up two days a week now: shoots, appearances, posts. His training is suffering. His agent says no player at his level turns down money.

choices.label: Cut back to the brands you believe in
choices.text: He keeps three and lets the rest go. His training improves. His agent sulks for a month.

choices.label: Hire a team to manage it
choices.text: A small team handles scheduling and content. His duty days shrink to one.

choices.label: Do it all
choices.desc: Make hay while the sun shines.
choices.text: He does it all. The money is extraordinary. His form isn't.

scenarios.title: Buy the Club?
scenarios.text: His first club, {FIRSTCLUB}, is in financial trouble. A lawyer suggests a crazy idea: buy it. Become the owner of the club where it all began.

choices.label: Buy it
choices.desc: Save the club that made you.
choices.text: He buys {FIRSTCLUB}. The town celebrates for a week. The finances are a nightmare. It's the best thing he's ever done.

choices.label: Invest a share
choices.text: He buys a minority stake. The club survives. He gets a seat on the board and a lot of phone calls.

choices.label: Donate, don't buy
choices.text: A large donation keeps the lights on. They name the youth stand after him.

scenarios.title: The Statue
scenarios.text: The club has commissioned a statue of him outside the stadium. The sculptor wants three sessions. The first clay model looks a bit like him and a lot like his uncle.

choices.label: Accept with humility
choices.text: The statue is unveiled in front of twenty thousand people. {MUM} touches its face and cries. It does look a bit like his uncle.

choices.label: Ask for a statue of the fans instead
choices.text: He asks them to sculpt the fans in the stands instead. The bronze crowd outside the stadium becomes the club's most-photographed spot.

scenarios.title: Global
scenarios.text: He lands in a country he has never visited, and people at the airport know his name. Kids in his shirt. A taxi driver with his face on a keyring. He is famous in places he can't find on a map.

choices.label: Spend a day with local kids
choices.text: He spends a day on a dusty pitch with a hundred kids. Somewhere among them is a future footballer who'll tell this story in thirty years.

choices.label: Stay in the hotel
choices.text: He rests. The fans camp outside the hotel anyway.

scenarios.title: 'He Owes Me'
scenarios.text: A former youth coach is telling journalists that {J} owes his whole career to him, and that he's never been thanked. It's partly true. It's mostly not.
scenarios.prompt: An old coach claims credit for your career.

choices.label: Thank him publicly anyway
choices.text: He thanks the coach in an interview. The coach goes quiet, then sends a kind message. It wasn't really about credit.

choices.label: Set the record straight
choices.text: He tells the real story. It's accurate and slightly ungracious. The story runs for a week.

scenarios.title: One of the Seniors
scenarios.text: Without anyone saying it, something has changed: the young players come to him for advice now, the senior players include him in the meetings with the manager, and nobody makes him carry the balls.

choices.label: Take the responsibility seriously
choices.text: He starts arriving earlier, checking on the young players, standing up in meetings. The squad notices.

choices.label: Stay the same
choices.text: He stays the same. Quiet, reliable. Some lead with words, some with presence.

scenarios.title: The Promise to {MUM}
scenarios.text: At nine years old, after a match in the rain, he promised {MUM} that one day she would never have to work again. She's still working. She says she likes it.

choices.label: Make her retire, with love
choices.desc: A monthly allowance and a holiday.
choices.text: He hands her a card that says 'You're retired.' She argues for a week, then goes on holiday and comes back a different woman.

choices.label: Let her keep working if she wants
choices.text: He tells her she never has to, and she chooses to. That was the promise, really.

scenarios.title: The Star Treatment
scenarios.text: He was late to training twice this week. A young player was late once and was fined and dropped. He wasn't. The dressing room has noticed the double standard.

choices.label: Ask the manager to fine you too
choices.text: He asks for the fine and pays it publicly. The young player gets his place back. The dressing room's respect is total.

choices.label: Enjoy it
choices.text: He enjoys it. The young players stop looking up to him.

scenarios.title: The Phone
text: No club. Every morning he trains alone in a public park. Every evening he checks his phone for messages from his agent. Some days there's nothing.
Free agency. He has a training plan, a cheap gym membership and too much time to think.

choices.label: Train like a professional anyway
choices.hint: When the call comes, be fit.
choices.text: 6am runs, gym, ball work, every day. When the call comes, he'll be ready.

choices.label: Accept a trial anywhere
choices.text: He tells his agent: any trial, anywhere. Two calls come within a week.

choices.label: Use the time for family
choices.text: He goes home and spends real time with his family for the first time in years. It's strangely the happiest month in ages.

scenarios.title: Famous for the Wrong Thing
scenarios.text: He has more followers than half the first team, mostly from a viral video, but he's barely played. The senior players have started calling him 'Influencer'.
scenarios.prompt: You're more famous online than on the pitch.

choices.label: Post less, train more
choices.text: He goes quiet online and works harder. A few months later, the nickname fades.

choices.label: Embrace it
choices.text: He keeps posting. The squad keeps teasing. The manager keeps him on the bench.

scenarios.title: Late Bloomer
scenarios.text: At an age when some players are at their peak, he's still waiting for his moment. Friends from the academy are playing abroad. He's beginning to wonder.

choices.label: Keep going
choices.text: He keeps going. Plenty of great players didn't break through until their mid-twenties. He might be one of them.

choices.label: Drop down a level to play every week
choices.hint: A step back to step forward.
choices.text: He tells his agent: a smaller club, where he'll play every week.

scenarios.title: Everyone Knows
scenarios.text: A newspaper has published his salary. The fans are debating whether he's worth it. A man on the radio says he earns more in a week than the man does in two years.

choices.label: Talk about it honestly
choices.text: He says he knows how lucky he is and talks about what he does with it. It lands well.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.text: He says nothing. For a month, every bad pass is followed by a chant about his wage.

scenarios.title: A Kid From Home
scenarios.text: A sixteen-year-old from his hometown has just signed his first contract and sent {J} a message: 'You're the reason I play. Any advice?'
scenarios.prompt: A kid who idolises you asks for advice.

choices.label: Call him and talk for an hour
choices.text: An hour on the phone: money, agents, family, injuries, staying humble. The boy writes it all down.

choices.label: Send a signed shirt and a short message
choices.text: A shirt and three sentences. The boy frames both.

scenarios.title: {Al} vs {DAD}
scenarios.text: {DAD} doesn't trust {A}. {A} thinks {DAD} interferes. Both have called {J} to complain about the other. Both are a bit right.
scenarios.prompt: Your agent and your father are at war.

choices.label: Back {Al} on business
choices.text: He backs {Al} on business decisions. {DAD} is hurt and stays away for a month.

choices.label: Back {DAD}
choices.text: He backs {DAD}. {Al} works with less enthusiasm afterwards.

out.text: Three hours, a lot of tea and some shouting. They come out with a grudging respect.
It goes badly. Now they both blame {J}.

scenarios.title: The Street Game
scenarios.text: Driving through a poor neighbourhood, he sees kids playing on a concrete pitch with a deflated ball. He tells his driver to stop.

choices.label: Join the game
choices.text: He plays for an hour in his expensive shoes. The kids can't believe it. Neither can he. It's the most fun he's had in months.

choices.label: Send them proper balls and a coach
choices.text: The next week, a van arrives with balls, nets, kits and a coach paid for a year.

scenarios.title: Not Playing, Not Leaving
scenarios.text: He's not playing, but the club won't sell him: his wages are high, the fee they want is higher. He's stuck, paid well, and miserable.
scenarios.prompt: You're stuck at a club that won't play or sell you.

choices.label: Offer to take a pay cut to leave
choices.text: He offers a cut. The club listens. A transfer becomes possible.

choices.label: Stay and fight for your place
choices.text: He keeps training brilliantly. The manager eventually has no choice.

choices.label: Go public
choices.text: His interview makes headlines. The club is furious. It also works: an offer comes in a month.

scenarios.title: The Club Can't Pay
scenarios.text: The club is in a financial crisis. The president asks the best-paid players to take a pay cut of a third for the rest of their contracts. Junior staff jobs depend on the answer.
scenarios.prompt: Take a big pay cut to save jobs?

choices.label: Take the cut, and say so publicly
choices.text: He takes the cut and announces it. The whole squad follows. Nobody at the club loses their job.

choices.label: Take the cut quietly
choices.text: He takes the cut quietly. The staff find out anyway, and the kit man hugs him in the corridor.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.text: He refuses. Two junior staff lose their jobs. Everyone knows why.
